investigations.question: When a follower installs a snapshot while its persisted log already ends above the snapshot's LastLogIndex, does the follower's last-log report allow the leader's next AppendEntries (PrevLogEntry = snapshot index) to be accepted, or does the leader loop re-transferring the same snapshot with no follower progress?
investigations.hypothesis: installSnapshot restores the FSM, sets lastApplied/lastSnapshot/configuration and compacts logs at or below req.LastLogIndex, but never truncates log entries above req.LastLogIndex and never calls setLastLog. The cached lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm therefore keep the stale suffix, so getLastEntry reports (staleLast, staleTerm) instead of (snapshotIndex, snapshotTerm) whenever lastLogIndex > lastSnapshotIndex. appendEntries then fails the PrevLogEntry==lastIdx branch and either logs.GetLog errors (entries compacted) or returns the stale term, so it rejects with NoRetryBackoff. The leader lowers nextIndex by one (resp.LastLog+1 is above nextIndex-1, so min picks nextIndex-1), and once nextIndex-1 falls below the leader's compacted first index setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound and the leader re-sends the identical snapshot.
investigations.discriminator: Run the same 3-node in-memory scenario twice: with the isolated node's pre-reconnect last log index below the replacement leader's snapshot index (control, no stale suffix) and above it (case, stale suffix). If the explanation holds the control converges after one install, while the case leaves the isolated node stuck at the snapshot index with leader commit index above it and repeated identical snapshot installs. If the case also converges, the stale-suffix explanation is refuted and the harness or predicate must be revisited.
counterevidence: The control branch (follower log at or below the snapshot index) reaches the leader commit index, so ordinary snapshot catch-up works; the violation is specific to a follower whose persisted log extends above the snapshot index.

The predecessor experiment's comparisons were unusable (all unknown) because its two mutually exclusive scenario_setup admissions could not both correlate to one result event; that encoding defect is corrected here and is not evidence about the target.
limitations: Single-process in-memory InmemTransport, FileSnapshotStore and InmemStore/MockMonotonicLogStore; network/TCP transports and disk-backed stores were not exercised.
Only live catch-up was observed; restart/recovery of a node left holding an above-snapshot suffix, and any consequence for committed entries or safety (as opposed to progress), were not tested.

TrailingLogs=0 forces compaction; with larger TrailingLogs the follower must be correspondingly further behind for the leader to send a snapshot, but the follower-side last-log state that causes the stall is unchanged.

Comparison 2 (applicability stale_suffix=true, store_monotonic=true, assertion stalled==false) evaluated event index 5 and is violated with valid witness index 5: case_monotonic_stall behaved identically (applied 45 vs leader commit 55, old_last_after=223, stalled=true) even though removeOldLogs deleted the above-snapshot bytes. Together with the source trace (installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 resets lastApplied/lastSnapshot/config and compacts or removes logs at or below req.LastLogIndex but never truncates above it or calls setLastLog; getLastEntry at state.go:167-174 keeps returning the cached above-snapshot index/term; appendEntries at raft.go:1475-1502 rejects the PrevLogEntry check; replicateTo at replication.go:222-260 walks nextIndex down to ErrLogNotFound and sendLatestSnapshot re-sends the same snapshot), this establishes the defect for both LogStore monotonicity branches.

answers.1b24d155db77414b9490619c49f7a51f-gap-0: Yes. CheckRun ed8023e758ae49bc93676179f4ae489c (completed, exit_code 0, no parsing errors, prerequisites matched) shows the monotonic store stalling exactly like the non-monotonic one. Comparison 2 (applicability stale_suffix=true, store_monotonic=true, assertion stalled==false) is violated with valid witness index 5: scenario case_monotonic_stall reports snapshot_index=45 < old_last_before=223, old_last_after=223, old_applied_after=45 while leader_commit_index=55, stalled=true, isolated_caught_up=false. Because MockMonotonicLogStore makes installSnapshot take the removeOldLogs branch, the above-snapshot bytes are already deleted, so what survives is the cached lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm, which is not reset (no setLastLog call) and is still reported by getLastEntry (state.go:167-174). The stall is therefore caused by the cached last-log state, not by retained log bytes.

knowledge.assertion: installSnapshot does not truncate log entries above req.LastLogIndex and does not call setLastLog
getLastEntry reports the cached log index/term whenever it is at or above the snapshot index
appendEntries rejects on a missing or term-mismatched PrevLogEntry without truncating
replicateTo lowers nextIndex and falls back to re-sending the newest snapshot on ErrLogNotFound

counterevidence: The monotonic branch confirms rather than refutes the explanation: deleting the above-snapshot bytes (removeOldLogs) did not restore catch-up, which rules out retained bytes as the necessary cause.
The control comparison still holds, so ordinary snapshot catch-up is unaffected.
The predecessor run's nonzero exit was an upstream helper shutdown timeout (testing.go:307) and is preserved as counterevidence for that failed attempt; it carried no target-behavior claim.
limitations: Only progress/liveness is established; no committed entry was observed to be lost or overwritten, so no safety violation is claimed.
Coverage is limited to the in-memory, single-process, 3-node configuration described in the experiment scope; network transports, disk-backed stores and restarts were not exercised.

latest_interpretation.report_answer: 在保留执行 CheckRun ed8023e758ae49bc93676179f4ae489c（completed，exit 0）中：对照场景比较成立（applied 55 = leader commit 55）；非单调存储对比 violated，witness 为事件 3（applied 冻结 45，leader commit 55，stalled=true）；单调存储（removeOldLogs 已删除快照索引以上的日志字节）对比同样 violated，witness 为事件 5（snapshot_index 45、old_last_before 223、old_last_after 223、applied 45、stalled=true）。因此问题不取决于日志字节是否保留，而在于 installSnapshot 未重置缓存的 lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm（未调用 setLastLog），getLastEntry 继续返回快照索引以上的旧项，AppendEntries 的 PrevLogEntry 校验被拒，leader 逐次下调 nextIndex 直至 ErrLogNotFound 并反复重发同一快照。范围限于单进程内存、3 节点；未测试重启恢复，也不主张已提交日志丢失。

knowledge.statement: (*Raft).installSnapshot restores the received snapshot into the FSM, sets lastApplied=req.LastLogIndex, sets lastSnapshot=(req.LastLogIndex,req.LastLogTerm), overwrites the latest and committed configuration, then removes or compacts only logs at or below req.LastLogIndex (removeOldLogs for a MonotonicLogStore, otherwise compactLogs). It never calls setLastLog and never truncates log entries above req.LastLogIndex, so the cached lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm retain any pre-existing suffix.
knowledge.conditions: A follower handles an InstallSnapshotRequest and its persisted log already contains entries at indices greater than req.LastLogIndex, for example an uncommitted suffix written by an earlier leader term.

knowledge.statement: (*raftState).getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, and returns (lastSnapshotIndex,lastSnapshotTerm) only when the cached log index is below the snapshot index. After a snapshot install that leaves a longer persisted log, the follower therefore reports the stale tail index and term rather than the snapshot index and term.
knowledge.conditions: lastLogIndex > lastSnapshotIndex on the local raftState, which holds after installSnapshot when the log was not truncated above the snapshot index.

knowledge.statement: (*Raft).appendEntries verifies a.PrevLogEntry by comparing it to getLastEntry; if they differ it reads logs.GetLog(a.PrevLogEntry). A missing entry or a differing term sets resp.NoRetryBackoff=true and rejects the request without truncating the local log.
knowledge.conditions: A follower receives an AppendEntriesRequest with a.PrevLogEntry > 0.

knowledge.statement: (*Raft).replicateTo advances s.nextIndex to max(min(s.nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1) on a rejected AppendEntries, so a follower that reports a higher LastLog than the leader's nextIndex causes nextIndex to decrease by one; when setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound it goes to SEND_SNAP and sendLatestSnapshot re-sends the newest snapshot and sets nextIndex=meta.Index+1 on success.
knowledge.conditions: The follower keeps rejecting AppendEntries and its reported LastLog stays above the leader's nextIndex.

knowledge.statement: In the retained 3-node in-memory execution, when the isolated node reconnected with its persisted log ending above the replacement leader's snapshot index (case: old_last_before=222 vs snapshot_index=45), the node's applied index stayed at the snapshot index 45 across the observation window while the leader's commit index was 55 (stalled=true, isolated_caught_up=false); in the same execution the control with the node's log ending below the snapshot index (old_last_before=25) reached applied index 55 and caught up (stalled=false, isolated_caught_up=true).
knowledge.conditions: Single process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with InmemStore and FileSnapshotStore, ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, TrailingLogs=0, replacement leader compacted at or below its snapshot index; the isolated node's above-snapshot suffix was produced by real uncommitted Apply calls on the old leader before it stepped down.

knowledge.statement: In the retained 3-node in-memory execution (CheckRun ed8023e758ae49bc93676179f4ae489c), the post-snapshot catch-up stall occurred for both log-store monotonicity branches: with a non-monotonic InmemStore the isolated follower stayed at applied index 45 while the leader commit index was 55 (event 3, stalled=true, isolated_caught_up=false), and with MockMonotonicLogStore, whose removeOldLogs deletes the above-snapshot log bytes during installSnapshot, it still stayed at applied index 45 with old_last_after=223 (event 5, stalled=true, isolated_caught_up=false). The control whose log ended at or below the snapshot index reached applied index 55 (event 1, isolated_caught_up=true).
knowledge.conditions: Single process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with FileSnapshotStore; ProtocolVersion=3; HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms; TrailingLogs=0; the isolated node's above-snapshot suffix was produced by real uncommitted Apply calls on the old leader before it stepped down; only live catch-up was measured.
